problem:
Disprove the following statement:

For any $a,b\in Z,$ if $6a≡6b\,(\text{mod}\,15),$ then $2a≡2b\,(\text{mod}\,15).$

To {{field-1}} a universal statement, it's sufficient to find {{field-2}}. 
In other words, we need to show that {{field-3}}

$$
{{field-4}}(\text{mod}\,15)\,\text{and}\,{{field-5}}(\text{mod}\,15).
$$

Let's choose

$$
a={{field-6}},\,b={{field-7}}.
$$

Then, $6a=$ {{field-8}} and $6b=$ {{field-9}}. 

Hence, we have that 

$$
{{30}_{⏟}}_{6a}{{field-10}}{{60}_{⏟}}_{6b}\,(\text{mod}\,15)\,\text{and}\,{{10}_{⏟}}_{2a}{{field-11}}{{20}_{⏟}}_{2b}\,(\text{mod}\,15).
$$

So, the pair $a=$ {{field-12}} and $b=$ {{field-13}} is our counterexample. Therefore, the given statement is false.
